reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is scientifically sound, correctly identifying force-constant disorder from mass, size, and electronegativity differences as a key driver of phonon scattering in single-phase HEAs, though the quantitative predictions (20% accuracy, 30% reduction) are speculative without a specific model framework.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and decisive, with a well-defined experimental benchmark comparing model-selected vs. conventionally-selected alloys, but the reliance on multiple advanced characterization techniques (inelastic scattering, APT) makes it highly resource-intensive.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is highly useful as it directly addresses the research question by proposing a concrete, mechanistic predictive strategy with clear falsification criteria, offering a valuable direction for researchers in thermal-insulation HEA design.
